description: Message intelligence: Turn your emails, slacks and coding chats into self-updating todo list

app_services.description: Email gateway for other apps: subscribe to a semantic slice of the user's mail (e.g. 'all invoices') and receive the LLM's answer per matching email, optionally with the original email and attachments shared — without your app needing any mail access of its own.

index.Description: The main dashboard, served from the SHARED SHELL page (shell.html + shell.js — one document hosting the Dashboard and To-dos views; switching between them is an in-page repaint over one loaded data set, with pushState keeping URLs/back-forward honest). This view: the persisted project board (manual edits persist), filterable via its own filter bar (min PROJECT importance + hide toggles + text search), board tools (expand/collapse all), and the due-date interpreter maintenance pass. Mail checking, the account picker, the ＋ Add… button and the email viewer are mounted once by the shell. Redirects to the setup page when no mail account is set up or training is unfinished.

recent.Description: TO-DOS, served from the SHARED SHELL page (see the index page entry) — every to-do of every project, sliced page-wide: tabs I owe / Team / Owed / Read (flat cross-project lists of the standard to-do rows), People (master-detail grouping of Owed/Team items by debtor), All To-dos (the archive), Messages (the mail history rendered with the Events page's cards), and Events (the 'what happened since I last checked?' digest with automation decisions and a Load-older button). Its own filter bar cuts ONE working set for every tab: timeframe on processed time, min-priority, “show only” restrictors, hide toggles and search. The ORDER is chosen separately, on a pill right-aligned on the section-title line under the tabs. Events come from the shell's shared windowed loader — switching views refetches nothing.

threads.Description: THREADS view of the shell (same shell.html/shell.js): every email thread / Slack conversation as a Mail-style summary row; choosing one opens the email viewer embedded as columns 2 + 3.

events.Description: Chronological MESSAGES, served from the SHARED SHELL page (see the index page entry) — a mail-client-like ruled list (newest first by the message's own date, grouped by day) of the events audit log: every analysed email, auto-processed message and manual edit, kind shown by the glyph disc (📧/⚙/✍️), with the tasks each raised/resolved as typed chips, badges, cost, and its own filter bar (min-priority, hide resolved/manual/auto, search). Any event opens the shared full-email viewer. Events come from the shell's shared windowed loader; Show more / Load older page the feed on.

people.Description: People directory, served from the SHARED SHELL page (see the index page entry): everyone from the analysed mail, with its own filter bar (min PERSON importance, bulk-sender toggle, sort, search) and a per-person meeting-prep detail view in sub-tabs under a header card with the rank control. Selection rides on the URL hash (#<address>) — deep links keep working. Manual rank (1-5) overrides the model's importance; the person editor here carries the on-demand 'Update with AI' re-profile (job when background-capable, in-tab otherwise). Tops the shell's shared events log up to 2000 rows for the message-history panels.

setup.Description: Onboarding + SETUP + status/prefs. A welcome hero gates on ONE input permission (mail OR messaging) plus llm, then: a mail account gets the first-run form (ONE mailbox, history window, model) and the ONE big AI pass (jobs/bootstrap/*) with correction rounds, saved via adopt.js; a MESSAGING-ONLY install instead gets the Slack channel picker inline (slackChannelsUi.js) — save the tracked conversations and the normal checks take over. Returning users land on the STATUS tab — since 2026-09-09 a RESOURCES layout: a left list of every source (mail accounts, Slack workspaces, AI agent stores) with its state (trained / training / saved / not started / needs re-authorisation / paused), and a right detail panel: the mail account panel (train / continue / pause / forget), or the channel module for a Slack row (slackChannelsUi, fixed to that workspace) / a work row (workSessionsUi, fixed to that store), each with the save-then-analyse-now-or-later offer — the Channels tab is gone. Then the RULES tab (all custom instructions at every scope), CONNECTED APPS and PREFERENCES. An agents-only install gets the AI agents picker inline on the welcome. New mail is NOT handled here — the dashboard does that.

cleanup.Description: The WEEKLY CLEAN-UP page (specs/superlazy-weekly-cleanup.md; not in the nav — the experimentation host, later also a Setup tab). One streamed model call over the app's current state (situation, standing instructions with usage, catalog with open + recently closed to-dos, people, gathering-dust and archive-candidate lists, the user's graded hand edits, earlier decisions) plus an INPUT WINDOW — by default an index of every analysed item across channels (optionally restricted to ticked accounts) with bodies fetched on the model's request, or full mail threads — returns SECTIONS: a period summary, a focus list for the horizon ahead, attention cards (summary + recommendation + the to-dos to act on), and proposals in the ops vocabulary for stale tasks, archiving, merges, splits/moves/restructures, people, standing rules and learned patterns, plus questions with optional actionable options. A rail of sections with undecided counts, Accept / Ignore / Accept all per section, Apply under the audit lock. To-dos everywhere render as the standard live task row (same modals as the other pages). Also: a size and cost estimate before sending, input vs output cost after, model picker, windows and thresholds saved as prefs, under-the-hood texts, free housekeeping passes, the archived-projects list with Restore, past runs.

styleguide.Description: Test page (not in the nav menu): the living style guide — renders every entity treatment (design tokens, cross-link chips, to-do rows, event rows, person avatars, the project card) through the REAL shared components with mock fixtures, for refining the per-entity visual identity before it is applied to the live pages.

slacklab.Description: DEV page (not in the nav): the Slack formation DRY RUN — build chunks over a chosen window WITHOUT persisting anything and review every chunk as a transcript, the user-resolution table (Slack id → display name / email / bot) and a volume & cost projection per conversation, for tuning chunking against a real workspace. Channel setup itself (the connection picker + conversation roster + Save selection) is the SHARED slackChannelsUi.js module, mounted here for convenience — its home is Setup & Prefs → Channels.

inspect.Description: DEBUG: analyse ONE message at a time with full wire visibility — the exact request (system prompt / cached catalog turn / volatile block), every LLM round (request_more, repair), the raw response, thinking, tokens incl. cache read/write, and cost — and NOTHING is persisted until the user presses Save (Ignore keeps the results on screen and leaves the cursor in place, so the same message can be re-run in another tab under different Preferences for A/B comparison). Holds the run lock while inspecting so a background run can never race the same message.

agentslab.Description: DEV page (not in the nav) for the WORK channel (specs/superlazy-sessions.md). Step 1 mounts the SAME channel-setup module the Setup page's Channels tab uses (workSessionsUi.js: fs store, ME, repos, first-read window, Save → the channel:'work' account record; the normal checks then read the sessions along with mail). Steps 2–3 are the dev tools: a formation DRY RUN (the exact turn items a run would queue, each openable as the viewer will show it plus its raw transcript records) and the ZERO-WRITE chronological run — the real analysis over every formed turn against an empty or the real catalog, painted with the real Events/project components, optionally SAVED to the database in one commit.

requestauditlab.Description: LAB / DEV TOOL (not in the nav): every LLM exchange the per-message engine made while recording was on (settings.llm_audit, toggled here or via superlazy.audit(true) in the Setup page console), grouped into request chains (analysis call + request_more detail rounds + repair rounds) per run, with the cost of each part (cached prefix read, new input, cache writes by TTL, output), the exact turns sent (cached durable turn loaded on demand from its blob), the reply, thinking and raw usage. Calls on $0 local connectors are priced as eq equivalents via the API price list. Records are pruned after llm_audit_days (default 3).

replay.Description: DEMO page: plays a recorded stretch of SuperLazy back at demo speed (default 0.25s per input) — the input arriving on top of the stage, the to-do list moving underneath (3 I owe / 3 Team / 3 resolved, each with a "+N more"). Criteria: from/to dates, channels, repos, projects, which event kinds count as a step. NO model calls, NO mail fetch, NOTHING written: steps come from the events log and the board is reconstructed from each to-do's created_asof + evidence[].changed diffs (replayEngine.todoAsOf). The stage is a fixed half-slide (or full-slide) frame with a Present button that scales it to fill the screen.

files.Description: Browser data layer for inter-app subscriptions: request intake from the message inbox into the subscriptions collection, the approve/deny/pause/resume/revoke lifecycle with status messages back to the requester, LLM prefilter derivation at approval, and the delivery flusher that shares originals then sends pending delivery records as inter-app messages.

The Connected apps tab on Setup & Prefs: shows each requesting app's server-verified identity and verbatim prompt, with approve/deny (plus prefilter suggestion), pause/resume/revoke, and delivery counts — the human consent surface for inter-app subscriptions.

Job-side core of inter-app subscriptions: loads active subscriptions per run (before durable-sig/pin adoption), builds the deterministic per-subscription detector lines for the cached durable turn, the cheap prefilter gate that rescues matching mail from the autopilot short-circuit, and the idempotent delivery writer + message sender used by the app_subscription workflow.

All rendering for the Setup page's bulk bootstrap (first-run) flow: the run bar and live progress (waiting/thinking/writing), the model's reasoning kept on screen, per-call diagnostics, the tab/sub-tab and banner state machines (the first section opens its tab, nothing auto-switches after that; saving stays locked until answers are sent or waived), progressive per-section rendering in the app's entity identity, and the correction controls whose notes go back with the next round.
Styles for the Setup page's bulk bootstrap flow: sticky run bar, banner, tabs and panels, project/person/autofile cards, question rows and the raw-output drawer.

The BULK BOOTSTRAP system prompt (BOOTSTRAP_PROMPT_VERSION) and the refinement-message builder: produces THE MAP — business context (written FOR the per-message analyst), project skeletons with their live to-dos, people profiles, per-sender autofile candidates and open questions — as a JSONL stream, cheap sections first, 'done' last. Its 'What a project is' paragraph is copied VERBATIM from jobs/analyze_thread/prompt.js (test-enforced).

Builds the mailbox dump: thread-grouped markdown, newest thread first / oldest message first, SHORT SURROGATE ids (m0001/th001, separate namespaces) with translation maps back to real ids, ME tagging, deterministic byte budget with graceful degrade, and the full bodies kept aside for fetch requests.

Turns the bootstrap MAP into the real stores — projects (with their to-dos, dated by the email that raised them, and partial_threads for threads cut by the window), people profiles, auto-file senders (the standing per-sender action the per-message workflow reads), settings (incl. the business context), the account record whose CURSOR is set one millisecond past the newest message read, and — for the emails the map actually QUOTED as evidence — their stored bodies plus one event each naming the to-dos they produced (the summary event says plainly that uncited mail was read together and not stored individually). Writes records indistinguishable from the ones the per-message engine would have written (same id minting, same shapes).

The bootstrap LLM calls: streaming JSONL section parser, the incremental assembler, the first pass, the refinement rounds (same cached conversation) and resume-from-partial, with auto-continuation when the output budget runs out and cost/meta merged across turns.

OFFLINE verification of the bulk-bootstrap modules (no server, no LLM, no personal data in the file; runs against the user's stored mail when present, otherwise a built-in synthetic mailbox): dump determinism and format, the surrogate↔real id round-trip, the prompt sync contract with analyze_thread/prompt.js, JSONL streaming/continuation/resume behaviour, and the Setup page's bootstrap html↔js↔css contract.

OFFLINE cost diagnosis: reads the events log from the local datastore and prints per-message spend (model, in/out/cache read/cache write tokens, fetch rounds) plus the measured REQUEST composition (request_profile: chars per section, snapshot size), then aggregates — cache efficiency, fetch-round overhead, biggest sections — so cost drift shows as a pattern, not a feeling. node test/costReport.mjs [N].

OFFLINE verification of the batch/cache/staleness-tier pipeline (specs/pipeline-walkthrough.md §5–§7): hydrates the real stores from the local datastore, checks catalog snapshot vs live delta, the FULL/BRIEF/DORMANT tiers, batch assembly and the missing-entry re-queue.

Offline proof of the concurrency rules: the merge/heal cases as unit checks, then healDuplicateProjects run read-only over the real stored projects to report duplicate project_ids. node test/verifyProjectMerge.mjs

OFFLINE proof of the task-history trail: what the analyzer records when it creates or changes a to-do (evidence diffs + the llm_* baselines), what a manual edit records, and that a burst of manual fiddling collapses into ONE evidence entry and one upserted event per field. node test/verifyTaskHistory.mjs

App-wide design tokens (:root custom properties, loaded FIRST on every page): neutrals, status colours, the importance 1-5 scale (mirrored in renderUtils.js IMP_COLORS), the canonical task-direction set, event-kind colours, and the project/person entity accents.

The per-entity visual-identity components (chips, task rows, avatars, event kind discs, importance badge + imp-fg/imp-bl utility classes), the shared thread-grouped message-history rows (pp-msg / pp-thread — messageHistory.js renders on every page), plus .sl-v2-scoped restyles of existing epv-/ev-/pp- classes that pages opt into; loaded right after tokens.css on every page. Carries the fenced 'TASK CHECKBOX — EXPERIMENT' block: task-row checkboxes are drawn by hand (white box, coloured border, coloured tick) to match .done-mark instead of the native accent-color solid fill; --task-check-on switches green↔blue and deleting the block restores the native control.

SHARED rendering primitives (sub-module, imported not listed in modules): element helpers, date formatters, the importance colour scale + badge, the four entity chips (project/task/event/person), the initials avatar, the event kind disc, and the shared task row (taskRowEl — its due slot shows the hint text only on the day it was written, the interpreted date after that). Also owns the shared reading of a task's HISTORY (evidenceTrailOf / evidenceSummary / evidenceLabel) and the task row's history strip: the FIRST and LAST todo.evidence entries as one comma-separated line, with a '+ N more' (N = total - 2) between them, each email-backed one opening THAT message in the thread viewer. The task NAME is a button that opens the task modal, like the △ does. Row anatomy (2026-08-25): checkbox · name (opens the task modal) + ✏️ (same modal) + history strip · due · [project pill] · priority · ✕ — the due date LEFT of the project chip, priority at the far right so a column of rows lines up. Hovering the NAME (not the whole row) slides the description/sub-tasks open under it; the ✏️ glyph replaced the retired △ everywhere (people wouldn't read a triangle as edit). The 'set by you' dot is absolutely positioned on the priority badge's corner so it adds no width. taskRowEl's showDirection opt puts, at the very front of the row (left of the checkbox), the ☑️/📥/👥/📖 direction mark — off by default (a direction-scoped tab already says it), on wherever the list mixes directions: the Events page's task rows, both 'All tasks' archives, and the tasks behind one email in the viewer. A row state change that REMOVES the row (resolve / reopen / cancel) wipes it shut before committing, so a quick second click cannot land on the row that slid up underneath; PRIORITY changes deliberately do NOT wipe — taskSort.js holds the order so the row keeps its place, and sliding a row that never moves was pure noise (user, 2026-09-01).

Very light sub-tasks inside a task, stored as flat checklist lines ('- [ ]' / '- [x]') in the plain-text description — no schema change. Parse/stats/toggle helpers, the textContent-only DOM renderer (hover-revealed checkboxes, done = grey + strikethrough, ticked rows restyle themselves in place), and wireBulletContinuation (textarea Enter continues a '- ' list, Enter on an empty bullet exits it). Used by taskRowEl's hover slide-open description panel and the task editor / add-form textareas. Ticks persist via a manual_edit (target todo, field description) that page listeners deliberately do NOT repaint on — a repaint would slam the open panel shut.
Styleguide test page body: intro note, click-feedback line, and the sections host (wrapped in the sl-v2 opt-in class).

Styleguide entry point: renders tokens swatches, cross-link chips, to-do rows, event rows, people avatars/rows and the project card through the real shared renderers with mock fixtures; clicks flash a note instead of acting.
Mock projects/todos/events/people (real record shapes) used only by the styleguide page.
Layout styles for the styleguide page only (sections, captions, token swatches, legend).

The shared shell page body (serves the index, recent, events AND people page keys): top bar + status + one container per view — Dashboard, Tasks, Events (full-width feed) and People — each with its own filter bar host, plus the hidden stubs for shared ui.js renderers. shell.js shows one container at a time.

Entry point of the shared shell page: reads the URL for the initial view (index/recent/events/people), switches views in place with pushState/popstate, and mounts every cross-view singleton exactly ONCE — setup guard, appStore load, the ui.js hooks, the manual-event listener, the email-viewer context, mail tools (+ status poller), the ＋ Add… button, visibilitychange and hashchange — dispatching repaints (and per-view person-editor options) to the active view. It also wires the ui.js injections that need the store: setProjectDeleter (the project editor's Delete — out of the working set and out of storage) and setHostRepaint (every card edit repaints the active view behind the modal).

The shell's ONE in-memory working set (createAppStore): loads projects/profiles/instructions/accounts/settings via persist.loadAll plus a single shared windowed events loader (base 1000, ensureEventCoverage/loadOlder for more), merges session-raised extra events, and reloads wholesale only when new data definitely exists — view switches reuse it untouched. Deliberately no browser storage (shared origin across freezr apps).

The DASHBOARD VIEW module of the shell page (createDashboardView): the project board with its own filter bar (min importance / hide toggles / search), expand-collapse-all board tools, the 'No projects yet' banner and the due-date interpreter pass — data and cross-view wiring come from the shell/appStore.

Page-side entry points for ingestion: runNewMailCheck (in-tab, blocking, keep-page-open) and startBackgroundRun (hands off to the freezr job, FIRE-AND-FORGET because POST /jobs/run blocks for the whole run). Both thin wrappers over jobs/analyze_thread/ingest.js.

Turns a stopped-run error into an actionable sentence (no LLM credit left / mail token expired / rate-limited / offline / unusable model output). Shared by the training page and the dashboard mail check so both explain a stop the same way.

The model chooser, labelled with each model's TOKEN PRICE from freezr.llm.ping ('$3 in / $15 out per Mtok'), cheapest first. Deliberately NOT a cents-per-email estimate: that depends on thread length, stored history, extra context rounds and re-profiles, so the REAL per-email cost is measured and shown after the fact instead (engine.js spendSummary). Shared by the first-run form, the Status tab's start-training form, the mid-run switcher and Preferences.

The background-status strip under the top bar (pure renderer — mailTools' poller drives it): live progress from the run lock, 'N messages processed' after a run lands, stalled-run recovery pointer, mail-token-expired warning, and the mode-off standing reminder. Also the clean-up RESULTS bar (above the strip, until clicked) and kind-aware busy text with a spinner.

The keep-this-page-open modal for in-browser processing runs: do-not-refresh warning, live progress bar, Recent/Events watch-along links (new window), background-jobs grant pitch when not capable, Stop button, beforeunload guard (setUnloadGuard also used by the training view's banner). Stays up until the run finishes.
Onboarding helpers: permission grants (use_mail, use_llm, run_job/schedule_job), APP_SETTINGS_URL / RESOURCES_URL, and getBackgroundCapability (delegates to backgroundMode.probeCapability).

The TASKS VIEW module of the shell page (createTasksView): owns the tab + filter state (timeframe/priority/search/hide/show-only), builds the cross-project working set (direction tabs, per-person grouping, archive, Messages, the Events digest) from the shared appStore, and paints it — persistence and shared handlers come from the shell. The SORT is not in the filter bar: it is a pill on the section-title line, right-aligned beside "I owe" / "Team owes" / …, cycling priority → date changed → date due → project (the filter bar says WHAT shows, not in what order). It also flags when a priority edit is HOLDING the order still (taskSort.js) and a click lets go and re-sorts. The filter bar's "show only" row (resolved / I owe / Team owes / Owed, in the tabs' own icons) restricts positively and composes with the hide toggles, so Hide-resolved + Only-resolved deliberately shows nothing.

Data + digest model for the Tasks page: the windowed events loader (createEventsLoader — pages newest-first, ensureSince/ensureCount/loadOlder), the processed-time clock, and buildDigest() — windowed events → stats, resolved, decisions, per-project stories.

DOM rendering for the Tasks page: the page tab bar, cross-project task lists, the People master-detail view (sortable person list + selected person’s items), the All-Tasks archive view, plus the Events tab's Resolved list, Automation-decisions section and project-activity narrative cards.

Styles unique to the Tasks page: the page tab bar, the People master-detail split (person list rows, sort toggle, detail card), All-Tasks section heads, Load-older button, and the Events-tab digest layout (section rows, project narrative cards).

SHARED filter bar under the top bar: composable slots (kind chips / timeframe presets All-past hour-since last night-custom via an X-hours-or-Y-days stepper popover, opening on PAST 2 HOURS / min-priority / selects / "show only" icon-toggles (the positive counterpart of hide: nothing pressed = no restriction, several = their union; it composes with hide rather than overriding it) / hide icon-toggles (☑️ resolved, ✍️ manual, ⚙ auto, ⏱ not due, 👥📥 not mine — a red no-entry ring overlays a hidden kind) / actions / search); pages own the state.
Styles for the shared filter bar (filterBar.js) — one row of grouped pill controls, used by every page that filters.

Shared top bar (all pages): logo + page title + right-aligned menu via renderTopBar(pageKey). For the shell page it also takes onNavigate (in-page view switching for menu items the shell hosts) and setActiveTopBarPage(key) repaints just the title + you-are-here marker, leaving the mounted topbar tools untouched.
Styles for the shared top bar (topbar.js).

The EVENTS VIEW module of the shell page (createEventsView): the reverse-chronological feed ordered by the message's own date, its filters (priority / hide resolved-manual-auto / search), lazy Gmail label-name resolution, and Show-more/Load-older paging over the shared appStore events loader.
eventClock — the analysis clock (the message's own date); eventsUi.js and the events view import it from here.

DOM rendering for the events page: day-grouped feed of Mac-Mail-style rows (bold sender; folders/cost/time/kind icon right-aligned; subject; summary; inline reply drafts; live task rows), manual-edit summaries, the auto-file decision cards' counter buttons, and the search matcher.
Styles unique to the events page (day headers, kind-coloured event cards, feed).

SHARED full-email viewer modal (Mac Mail-style reading pane): message list rail + reading pane with a Reply / Reply all / Forward toolbar (Reply for Slack chunks), avatar header, the message's tasks and its sanitised body; replies open the shared composer inline; prefer_latest lands on the thread's newest message.

A small DOM-only markdown renderer (headings, lists incl. task items, fenced code, tables, blockquotes, inline bold/italic/code/strike, http(s)/mailto links) for agent-written plans and documents shown in the item modal. Untrusted input: builds nodes, never innerHTML; unsafe link schemes render as text. Imported by emailViewer.js — not a page module.

Shared modal shell (openModalShell): overlay + box + ✕ with a STACK so modals layer (email viewer on top of the project modal on top of the page); Escape closes only the topmost, z-index rises per level, overlay carries sl-v2 for entity styles. guardOutsideClick (text-entry editors): a stray outside click only pulses the box — closing from outside takes a double click. Opening a modal also moves FOCUS into it (and off the trigger): otherwise the clicked element keeps focus behind the overlay, tabbing starts outside the modal, and closing with Escape paints a :focus-visible ring on the trigger.

The project EDIT modal (✏️ on an expanded card): rename, set priority 1-5, merge into another project, DELETE the project outright (a two-step button at the FAR LEFT of the footer, with Done at the far right so the irreversible action is nowhere near the dismiss button: the first click arms it into "⚠ Are you sure? You cannot undo this action", only the armed click deletes, and it disarms itself after a few seconds — offered only where the page wired ui.js setProjectDeleter), and bulk select/resolve via RIGHT-side blue selection checkboxes. Each task's ✏️ opens THE SHARED task editor (taskEditor.js) stacked on top — no inline mini-form of its own any more. Mutations go through ui.js ops (manual_edit events + persistence). It is about the PROJECT only — the task list, its selection checkboxes and its bulk resolve were removed (2026-08-21) as a thinner duplicate of the card sitting right behind the modal.
The "+ Add Project" create modal on the dashboard: name + priority, then the new project opens on its "+ Add" tab.

THE ONE task edit modal (△ on any task row, and the project editor's per-task ✏️): staged rename / details / due date (live interpretation to a machine window) / priority 1-5 / ownership+who (known-people autocomplete after 2 letters; comma-separate joint owners; blank = unassigned), plus a collapsed searchable project picker to move the task or create a new project — applied on Save through ui.js taskEditOps. Outside clicks only pulse the box (double-click, Cancel, ✕ or Escape close it). Save / Cancel sit ABOVE the history (a long trail used to push them off the bottom of the modal). Below them it renders the task's full HISTORY — every todo.evidence entry newest-first with its field-level diff, the writer's reason and the model's message summary; entries backed by an email open that exact message in the shared thread viewer. Needs NO query: evidence travels on the project record. A manual priority override in that history offers 'revert to N' — restores llm_importance and unlocks the field, handing it back to the model (ui.js taskEditOps.revertImportance). The Priority row carries '↩ revert to automated priority N' beside its 'set by you' note — ONE action that drops the lock and restores llm_importance together; the number is omitted when the analyzer has not priced the task since that field existed, and the value then waits for the next analysis.

THE shared due-date control: a text box, the asap / today / tomorrow / next wk quick-fills (resolved synchronously through the deterministic parser — no LLM call), and the interpreted machine window in small print under it. Used by BOTH the task editor modal and the project card’s "+ Add" tab, so adding a task and editing one are the same experience.
Due-date interpreter: free-text due hints → machine window { due_earliest, due_latest } (ISO dates) via a deterministic parser with an LLM fallback; single and batch (migration) variants.

THE task-list sort keys, and the HOLD that keeps a list still while you re-price it: lastTouchOf plus sortImportanceOf / sortTouchOf, which every task list (recent.js, expandableProjectView.js) sorts through. ui.js calls holdSortKeys the instant before a priority edit lands, freezing that row’s keys so it keeps its place instead of jumping out from under the cursor; isSortHeld drives the sort control’s "out of order" flag and releaseSortHold (a sort-control click, a tab switch, a reload) lets go.

Builds the email viewer's shared superlazy context for any page: project-wide related messages, per-email tasks, still-relevant drafts, send capability, and sendMail — one implementation for Dashboard/Recent/Events/People. Also DURABLY retires suggested-reply drafts once the events log shows the user replied on the thread after the draft was made (retireStaleDrafts, run whenever the log loads).

SHARED thread-grouped message-history view (sub-module): one summary row per analysed email (kind disc, ←/→/· direction mark, date, subject, what-it-changed), threads collapsed under their newest message; plus projectHistoryEntries (the mail behind one project). Used by the People detail's Messages tab and the project card's Messages tab; styles in entities.css.

The person EDIT modal (person chips on expanded cards + ✏️ on the People page): edit the profile description + user_tone (a hand-edit locks the text against auto-overwrite), see the profile's lifecycle status (provisional, or grounded from full history), trigger the on-demand AI re-profile, and manage RULES for this sender (instructions collection — add scope=sender, or scope=domain via the 'everyone at this domain' checkbox; ALSO lists the domain/all-mail rules that apply to them read-only, with a pointer to Setup & Prefs → Rules where all scopes are managed).

The PEOPLE VIEW module of the shell page (createPeopleView): person view models (peopleData.buildPeople) from the shared appStore, hash-driven selection, its filter bar (importance/bulk/sort/search), the rank + profile-history edit path, and the on-demand AI re-profile (background job when capable, in-tab otherwise).

Pure aggregation for the People page: per-person view models (open items by direction, shared projects, thread-grouped message history incl. sent mail via events.to_addresses, responsiveness), search / min-importance / sort / bulk-sender filtering, and the plain-text meeting brief.

DOM rendering for the People page: list rows and the person detail panel — a header card (name, rank control, meeting brief) over SUB-TABS in the project card's tab language: Profile (summary/tone/stats/fit), I owe / Owed / Team / Read (standard task rows + that direction's resolved), Projects (live cards) and Messages (the shared thread-grouped history, messageHistory.js).
Styles unique to the People page (toolbar, list rows, detail cards, rank dots, direction groups).

PERMANENT core: builds the per-message request — people (ME tagged, no role seeds), linked projects' full to-do lists, the catalog of other active projects, the prior-message index, the replied-to parent in full (plus the latest message on a fork), the new message in full, plus any request_more detail. SIZE CAPS: message bodies are capped (new message 24k chars, inlined parent 6k, request_more detail 24k), the prior-message index keeps the 60 most recent, and a whole-request budget (70k chars) trims the new body further if the parts still add up. Every cut is MARKED in the prompt so the model knows to use request_more, and assemble returns a `size` diagnostic. REDUCTION LADDER: the request is built at a detail level and rebuilt leaner until it fits prefs.analysis_context_chars (DEFAULT_CONTEXT_CHARS / CONTEXT_CHOICES, exported for the prefs form). Reduction is by RELEVANCE TIER, not text truncation: suggested replies + resolved to-dos go first, then per-to-do prose, then the catalog's summaries (it becomes a name+id list), then people's profile prose (everyone stays listed; the sender + user keep full detail), then index lines. Every to-do id, person and project NAME survives at every level so the model can never duplicate what it could not see; only message bodies are character-capped. Returns a `size` diagnostic with per-section char counts.

PERMANENT core: the single LLM call (freezr passed in); parses + validates the output, returning either an analysis or a request_more, with one repair retry. The repair round is a CONVERSATION (prompt + the model's broken reply + a fix instruction), not a re-ask, so the model can repair its own output; a reply detected as truncated gets more output room and an instruction to be terser. The invalid-output dump labels the model's reply and OUR prompt unambiguously and collapses both. Output ceilings are 16k tokens (24k on a repair) — providers bill tokens generated, not the cap, so a low ceiling only buys truncated JSON. An EMPTY reply is handled specially: no empty assistant turn (providers reject it) and the retry drops responseType so the reply comes back as plain text.

PERMANENT core: applies the model's projects-nested OUTPUT to the project store — mints ids (maps tmp_id), MERGES the to-do + response + participant deltas (omission preserves), carries forward fields the render doesn't round-trip, reassigns moved to-dos, maintains evidence, enforces invariants, computes latest_delta + new/changed sets. Evidence entries now carry the field-level diff (`changed[]`), and the model's own values are stamped onto llm_importance / llm_short_description / llm_description so a later manual edit is distinguishable from — and revertable to — the machine's reading. The per-message diff is returned as todo_edits for the event record.

THE HUMAN GUARD (autopilotVeto / looksMachineAddress): the app REFUSES to put a sender on autopilot when they look like a person — vetoed if the user has ever written to them (you don't reply to a robot) or if the address is not machine-shaped AND the mail system doesn't label the message as bulk. Checked in onTrigger (blocks learning; the filed item stays) AND in shortCircuit (so a sender wrongly learned earlier stops being auto-filed and self-heals), never overriding a user-LOCKED choice. The prompt's sender test is the first line of defence; this is the second, because a standing decision that hides someone's mail is too sticky to leave to a prompt.

permissions.name: run_training_job
permissions.description: Run SuperLazy's mail-analysis job in the background on demand — lets training continue without keeping the browser window open.

permissions.name: schedule_training_job
permissions.description: Run SuperLazy's mail-analysis job automatically on a recurring schedule, so new mail keeps being analysed when the browser is closed.

permissions.name: read_archive
permissions.description: Read your Email Cabinet archive (message metadata + the stored EML files) so superlazy can analyse your threads.

permissions.name: use_ai
permissions.description: Use your LLM API keys to analyse threads (used from the next step onward; not exercised by the step-0 probe).

permissions.name: read_account_email
permissions.description: Read your connected mail account(s): the account email address (to pre-fill the 'you' field) and — when you choose 'Live mail' as the source — your messages, so superlazy can analyse them. Read-only; nothing is sent or modified.

permissions.name: send_replies
permissions.description: Send a suggested reply draft from your connected mail account — only when you press Send on it. Nothing is ever sent automatically.

permissions.name: messaging_read
permissions.description: Read messages from your connected messaging accounts (e.g. Slack) — conversations you choose to track are analysed into the same projects and to-dos as your mail. This permission is read-only; replying from superlazy is the separate send_messages permission.

permissions.name: send_messages
permissions.description: Reply on Slack from superlazy: post your reply in the conversation or thread you are reading. Nothing is sent unless you press Send.

permissions.name: msg_subscribers
permissions.description: Send subscription results (status updates and matching-email deliveries) to apps whose requests YOU approved on the Connected apps tab. Nothing is ever sent for a request you have not approved.

permissions.name: share_originals
permissions.description: Share a matched email (and later its attachments) with the app you approved on the Connected apps tab — per-record only, never table-wide.

permissions.name: read_work_sessions
permissions.description: Read the session transcripts your AI coding agent (Claude Code) leaves on this computer, so the work you did — and left unfinished — in those sessions is digested into the same projects and to-dos as your mail. Only prompts, recaps and the names of changed files are read into the analysis; tool output is dropped and token-like strings are scrubbed. Read-only.

subscriptions.description: Inter-app email subscriptions (specs/interapp-subscriptions.md): one record per request another app sent superlazy, mirrored from the message inbox by subscriptionsData.intakeRequests with a deterministic _id (sub_<hash of requester app + request ref>). The user approves/denies on Setup & Prefs → Connected apps; active records drive the app_subscription workflow's detector lines.

sub_id.description: Deterministic id, equals the record _id; referenced by LLM triggers and delivery records

requester_app.description: The requesting app's id — taken from the message's server-verified app_id, never from the payload

request_ref.description: The requester's own request record id (its record_id in the request message) — edits and cancellations key on it

label.description: Short name the requester chose, shown on the approval card

prompt.description: The requester's verbatim request (condition AND return format in one), length-capped; shown to the user and injected wrapped into the analysis prompt

include_original.description: true/false — whether approved deliveries also share the original email (and later attachments)

requested_hash.description: Hash of prompt+include_original as last requested; a mismatch with approved_hash sends the subscription back to pending

approved_hash.description: Hash of what the user actually approved

prefilter.description: Deterministic gate { subject_keywords, attachment_types, from_domains, has_attachments } derived at approval (user-editable) — a hit rescues the message from the autopilot short-circuit so the LLM can judge the real condition

status.description: pending | active | paused | denied | revoked | cancelled

status_reason.description: Human-readable note for the current status

subscription_deliveries.description: One record per matched email per subscription — written idempotently by the app_subscription workflow (deterministic _id del_<sub_id>_<hash(account|msg)>), then sent to the requester as an inter-app message (immediately when possible, else flushed by subscriptionsData.flushDeliveries). The record is the source of truth; the message is the transport.

sub_id.description: The subscription this delivery belongs to

delivery_id.description: Equals the record _id; the requester dedups on it (messages may be re-sent)

payload.description: The LLM's output to the requester's prompt, VERBATIM — opaque to superlazy

email_meta.description: { from, subject, received_at, msg_id, thread_id, account_id } — provenance only; ids are inert for the requester

shared.description: Refs to app-shared originals { email_body: {table_id, record_id}, files: [] } — set at flush time when include_original was approved (needs the freezr app-grantee change)

projects.description: One record per project — the cross-thread home of the to-do list. To-dos and suggested responses are EMBEDDED (always read/written together with their project). Mirrors the in-memory projectStore record; hydrated at startup via projectStore.hydrate().

project_id.description: Stable short id (p_xx) referenced by the model, todos, and the file_to_project auto-process target on profiles

summary.description: One-line roll-up of where the effort stands

llm_name.description: The analyzer's last automated copy of the name — same contract as llm_summary.

llm_summary.description: The analyzer's LAST AUTOMATED COPY of the summary (stamped by reconcile; manual edits never touch it) — summary !== llm_summary means the user overrode it, and the project editor offers the AI version back.

keywords.description: 3-7 precise, search-worthy tags maintained by the model (lowercase, deduped, max 10) — for matching future mail to this project (incl. after completion) and finding similar projects

importance.description: Effective importance 1-5 (number; user override when locked, else computed)

computed_importance.description: Max importance of open to-dos (number; shown even when locked)

importance_locked.description: Boolean — user set the importance; the model may not override

participants.description: STORED as an array of { address, role: me|team|external, role_note, last_updated_asof } (field names can't contain dots, and addresses do); persist.js converts to/from the in-memory address-keyed object

participant_emails.description: Flat searchable array of participant addresses (keys of participants)

todos.description: Embedded to-do objects: todo_id, direction (i_owe_them|they_owe_me|team_owes|read_only), short_description, description, sender, owner/owners/counterparty/counterparties (written by whoMapping.js from the model's `who` list — one person or several, lead first; 2026-09-19), importance (+importance_locked), status (open|in_progress|resolved|cancelled), due_hint (+due_earliest/due_latest ISO window), due_demote (USER-ONLY 1–3: hold the priority down by N until the due window opens — dueDates.effImportance; the model never sets it and reconcile carries it forward), change_reason, created/resolved/edited_asof. evidence[] is the task's WHOLE HISTORY and needs no query — one entry per thing that ever happened to it: { type (email|manual), source, thread_id, msg_id, asof, reason, who (the actor: the analysed message's sender, or 'you'), summary (the model's one-sentence read of that message), changed[] ({ field, from, to }) }. Manual edits COALESCE: every field change within 60s of the last one folds into the SAME entry (ui.js recordTodoChange), so ten rephrasings of a description are one line saying what actually changed. llm_importance / llm_short_description / llm_description are the MODEL'S last values for those fields, stamped only when the model itself emits them — a manual edit never touches them, so `importance !== llm_importance` IS 'the user overrode the machine', and they are what a revert-to-the-LLM's-reading would restore.

responses.description: Embedded suggested replies: response_id, todo_id, kind (answer|delegate|reminder), to/cc, subject, body, reminder_at, status (new|edited|sent|dismissed). A reply is only SHOWN while its todo_id points at a still-open to-do (expandableProjectView.isLiveResponse) — resolving the task retires its drafts; nothing is deleted, so reopening the task brings them back.

thread_ids.description: Threads linked to this project (cached hint, not a rule)

partial_threads.description: Thread ids whose earlier messages fell OUTSIDE the window the project was built from — what was read of them is a fragment, so the app can say 'history incomplete' rather than implying it saw the whole story. The email modal fetches the full thread live.

sources.description: Provenance — which source(s) fed this project, as 'email:<mail account address>' (union; a project touched by two accounts carries both). Set on every persisted step; enables the per-account 'Forget this account's data' action (persist.deleteAccountData) which deletes a project only when removing one account leaves it with no source. Records written before tagging existed have an empty array and are never removed by that action.

last_active_asof.description: Unix ms (number) — recency for the catalog

profiles.description: One record per person (keyed by lowercased email): the STABLE profile plus observed interaction stats. interaction_data is regenerable from the events log / archive (see specs/pipeline-backlog.md).

profile.description: { summary, relationship, responsibilities (a LIST of { id, text, source:'user'|'model', locked, asof } — one entry per kind of work; a source:'user' entry is the user's own words and is NEVER rewritten or dropped by the inline analysis, the re-profiler or a clean-up proposal; a legacy STRING is upgraded to one model-owned entry on load by jobs/analyze_thread/responsibilities.js, the only module that reads the shape), user_tone (how the USER writes to this person — learned by the re-profiler, voices suggested replies), llm_importance 1-5, responsiveness_note, auto_processes (array of standing per-sender actions — see jobs/analyze_thread/autoProcess.js: each { type, active, details, locked, suggested, source, asof }; the first type is file_to_project with details { project_id — a standard bucket OR any project of the user's, disposition — the automated-mail category when category-based }; active is THE explicit flag: future mail from this sender is handled without the LLM; locked means the USER set it and the model may never change it, its dissent lands in suggested; legacy records instead carry flat auto_file/auto_file_locked/disposition/auto_file_project_id/suggested_disposition fields, upgraded on load), last_profiled_asof, solidified_asof (set by the graduation re-profile; null = still PROVISIONAL — inline analysis may refine freely), user_edited (the user hand-edited the text; the model may never auto-overwrite it) }

manual_rank.description: Number 1-5 or null — user-set; OVERRIDES llm_importance absolutely

interaction_data.description: Observed stats (numbers): messages_from, messages_to, replies_by_user + reply_ms_by_user (user's reply count + total response time to this person), replies_by_them + reply_ms_by_them (their replies to the user), first/last_seen_asof. Averages derived; regenerable.

sources.description: Provenance — which source(s) this person was learned from, as 'email:<mail account address>' (union; someone seen on two accounts carries both). Same role as projects.sources: it is what makes the per-account 'Forget this account's data' action possible without touching people the other accounts also know.

stub.description: Boolean — true until a real profile_update lands

profile_history.description: Append-only archive of REPLACED profile versions — every time a solidified (or user-edited) profile's text / tone / priority is superseded by a re-profile, a manual edit, or a rank change, the outgoing version is snapshotted here (provisional pre-solidification refinements are NOT archived). One record per replacement; never updated.

responsibilities.description: The archived responsibilities — the entry LIST as it was (or a legacy string / null on old records)

manual_rank.description: Number 1-5 or null — the user-set rank at the time

user_edited.description: Boolean — the archived text had been hand-edited

profiled_asof.description: Unix ms — when the archived version was written

solidified_asof.description: Unix ms — when the profile first solidified (null = it was user-edited pre-solidification)

source.description: What replaced it: reprofile:graduation | reprofile:drift | reprofile:user_request | manual_edit | manual_rank

replaced_asof.description: Unix ms — when this version stopped being current

instructions.description: User-authored custom instructions (rules the LLM applies verbatim), scoped to a sender, a domain, one mail account, or all mail. Managed on the Setup & Prefs RULES tab (all scopes) and the person edit modal (sender/domain).

match.description: The email (scope=sender), @domain (scope=domain) or account_id (scope=account); ignored for all

text.description: The instruction, injected verbatim into the analysis prompt

author.description: 'user', or 'model' when a clean-up proposal added it and the user accepted

history.description: earlier versions [{ text, scope, match, asof }] when a clean-up rewrote or rescoped the rule

edited_asof.description: ms timestamp of the last rewrite / rescope / disable

origin.description: 'responsibility' when the instruction was made from a line on a person's card (person editor button); absent for instructions the user wrote

origin_address.description: the person whose card line it was made from (origin = responsibility)

origin_resp_id.description: the id of that line in the person's profile.responsibilities — editing the line rewrites this instruction, removing it disables it

origin_text.description: the card line's text when the instruction was last written from it

events.description: One record per analysed input (message or mailbox action): the audit log of how each message was dealt with — for debugging, the what-just-changed UI, and future learning jobs (e.g. regenerating interaction_data or profiles). Message events also carry the profile-lifecycle signals (profile_updates / reprofiles, slim), and each dedicated re-profile writes its own kind='reprofile' event ({ address, trigger, outcome, reason, cost }) — but the full REPLACED profile versions live in profile_history, which is never pruned; events are signals, profile_history is the archive. Pruned regularly per the events_retention_days setting. IDEMPOTENT IDS (specs/pipeline-walkthrough.md §2 and §11): analysis events (kind message/workflow_short_circuit/skipped) use the deterministic _id ev_<msgid>_<hash(account|msg)> — exactly one per (account, message), written AFTER analysis so its existence marks the message handled; re-processing (e.g. after a stale-lock takeover) upserts over it rather than duplicating. Concurrency is prevented up front by the single run lock, so there is no pre-LLM claim stub. Phase 2 mail_action events use evact_<msgid>_<action>_<hash incl. provider change id> — many per message, replay-safe. Two AUTO-FILE DECISION kinds exist to keep automation counterable rather than silent: 'autofile_learned' is written ONCE, the first time a sender is put on autopilot (from then on their mail is filed with no LLM read at all), and 'autofile_mismatch' when an already-learned sender's mail carries a label disagreeing with the learned category. Both carry importance 4 so they outrank the importance-1 item the auto-file created, and both are deliberately NOT counted as 'auto' by the Events page's hide-auto filter — they are the events that let the user overrule the automation.

msg_id.description: The analysed message's id (or the acted-on message for mailbox actions)

account_id.description: The mail account the message belongs to (part of the event's deterministic identity — msg_ids are only unique per account)

channel.description: The input item's channel — mail | messages | notes | calendar (specs/superlazy-inputs.md). Absent on records written before prompt 0.29 = mail.

action.description: PHASE 2 (mail_action kind): the semantic mailbox action — marked_read | flagged | trashed | deleted | marked_spam | archived | moved_folder

effects.description: PHASE 2 (mail_action kind): [{ todo_id, change }] — what the signal did (e.g. resolved a read-only item)

asof.description: Unix ms (number) — the message's date (the analysis clock)

kind.description: message | workflow_short_circuit | skipped | manual_edit | mail_action | reprofile | autofile_learned | autofile_mismatch | autofile_off | cache_refresh

latest_delta.description: { new_for_me, new_for_team, new_todo_ids, resolved } as applied

role_changes.description: Per-project participant role changes applied on this step

subject.description: The analysed message's subject (denormalised for the events feed)

summary.description: The model's ONE-sentence summary of what this message says/does (message_summary in the analysis output) — shown on the events feed, project activity, and the email modal; null for pre-0.15 events and non-LLM kinds

from_address.description: The analysed message's sender address (denormalised for the events feed)

to_addresses.description: Lowercased to+cc addresses of the analysed message — lets per-person views attribute SENT mail to its recipients

body_snippet.description: A short (~800 char) plain-text extract of the analysed message's body (clean_text), denormalised onto the event so the reader can show something INSTANTLY from the feed query — before the full body loads from email_bodies. Not the full body; that lives in email_bodies keyed by (account, msg).

via_workflow.description: Auto-process action keyword when the message was handled without the LLM, else null

autoprocess_blocked.description: When the sender carries an active auto-process yet this message was LLM-analysed: the gate that blocked the short-circuit (pref off / custom instruction / missing target). Older events stored it as autofile_blocked.

cost.description: USD cost of this message IN TOTAL (number) — every request_more round plus any re-profile it triggered; see cost_analysis / cost_reprofiles for the split. Before per-message accounting landed this held only the last LLM call's cost.

duration_ms.description: Number — wall-clock ms this ONE message took end to end (assemble + every LLM call + reconcile + triggers).

llm_calls.description: Number — how many LLM calls this message needed (1 normally; more with request_more rounds or a re-profile).

tokens.description: Per-message token usage: { input, output, other (e.g. cache reads), total } summed across every call this message made.

request_profile.description: What the analysis REQUEST was made of, measured at assembly: { volatile_chars, sections (chars per section: linked/newMessage/people/updates/…), reduce_level, snapshot_chars, snapshot_projects, prior_turns, rounds } — the record cost diagnosis reads instead of re-guessing

cost_analysis.description: Number — the analysis share of `cost` (all request_more rounds).

cost_reprofiles.description: Number — the share of `cost` spent on re-profiles this message triggered.

model.description: The model that analysed this message, as the provider reported it.

error.description: Step error message, when the analysis failed

importance.description: The EVENT's own priority 1-5 (number). EVERY event ranks, so every event can be dropped by a min-priority filter: mail that was auto-filed WITHOUT being read (workflow_short_circuit) and the standing auto-file DECISIONS about it (autofile_learned / autofile_mismatch) rank with the PROJECT they file into — a newsletter landing in a priority-1 bucket is a 1; SuperLazy's own housekeeping (cache_refresh / reprofile) ranks 1. Both the Recent digest and the Events min-priority filter prefer this over the touched to-do's importance; the Events feed also derives the same rank live (eventsUi.eventImportance), so records written before this stamp still filter correctly. Absent on ordinary analysed messages, which rank by the to-dos they raised.

address.description: The person this event is ABOUT rather than from (reprofile / autofile_learned / autofile_mismatch): the sender whose profile or auto-process changed.

category.description: autofile_learned / autofile_mismatch: the automated-email category the sender is filed under (newsletter | admin | admin_actions | social | promotions).

by_label.description: autofile_mismatch only: the category the MAIL SYSTEM's own labels imply, which disagrees with the learned one — the free drift signal that a sender straddles categories (e.g. a bank sending both payment alerts and promotions).

target_name.description: autofile_learned only: the name of the project/bucket this sender's mail will be filed into from now on.

project_id.description: The project this event concerns (a manual_edit's target, or the bucket an auto-file decision / auto-processed message filed into — the feed renders it as the row's project pill).

trigger.description: reprofile only: what caused it (graduation | drift | user_request).

reason.description: reprofile only: the model's explanation of what it changed and why.

doubt.description: autofile_mismatch only: the standing decision was applied but a guard disagreed (e.g. the sender is not a recognised machine address) — the mail WAS filed and this is the prompt to confirm or stop it; ignoring it is a valid answer.

direction.description: manual_edit bulk resolves only: the ONE direction bucket that was cleared (i_owe_them | team_owes | they_owe_me | read_only) when the user used a per-bucket “✓ resolve all” instead of the project-wide one. Absent = the whole project was resolved.

todo_edits.description: Field-level diffs this message applied to to-dos: [{ project_id, todo_id, field, from, to }] over importance / short_description / description / direction / due_hint / status (text values capped at 300 chars). Deliberately SEPARATE from `changes`, which drives the Recent/Events feeds — a priority nudge belongs in the audit trail, not as its own feed row. Nothing renders this today; it exists so 'what did the LLM set, and what did the user change afterwards' stays answerable when a detailed change view is built.

manual_id.description: manual_edit events only: the stable id (todo_id + burst seq + field) that persist.addEvent upserts on, so a burst of manual fiddling on ONE field inside the 60s coalesce window (ui.js COALESCE_MS) is one record whose `before` is the value the burst started from and whose `after` tracks the latest — instead of ten rows for one decision.

rules_offered.description: Standing-instruction ids that were in this request’s prompt (null when none).

rules_applied.description: Standing-instruction ids the model says actually changed this analysis (null when none).

email_bodies.description: LEGACY (read-fallback only since Phase 2 of specs/superlazy-inputs.md — new captures write to `inputs`; this table is dropped at the full reset). A stored SNAPSHOT of an analysed message's full body, captured for free during ingestion (the analyser already fetched the bytes). Lets the email reader show the real message from the app's own db — instantly and without hitting the mail provider — so live fetches are reserved for attachments / inline images only. One record per (account, message); _id is body_<msgid>_<hash(account|msg)>, matching the events id scheme (msg_ids are only unique per account). Treated as a PRUNABLE CACHE, not a source of truth: the mail provider remains authoritative, and the thread may have grown since capture (see captured_asof).

msg_id.description: The message's id within its account/source

account_id.description: The mail account (part of the record's identity — msg_ids are only unique per account)

thread_id.description: Its thread — the reader queries this to rebuild the thread rail from stored bodies

body_html.description: The message's HTML body as captured (may be empty; dropped when over the store cap — see html_truncated). Untrusted content: the reader MUST sanitize + Shadow-DOM it, never innerHTML directly. Inline cid: images will be broken until fetched live / from Mail Cabinet.

body_text.description: The message's plain-text body (or html→text fallback). Always kept even when body_html is dropped, so there is always something readable.

has_attachments.description: Boolean — whether the message carries attachments / inline images

attachments.description: Attachment MANIFEST only — [{ id, filename, mimeType, sizeBytes }]. The bytes are NOT stored; they are fetched on demand (live provider, or faster from Mail Cabinet when installed) only when the user opens one.

html_truncated.description: Boolean — body_html exceeded the store cap (~256KB) and was dropped; body_text was kept

captured_asof.description: Unix ms (number) — when this snapshot was stored. The reader shows an 'as of' note and can offer a live refresh, since the thread may have grown since.

inputs.description: One record per INPUT ITEM across all channels (specs/superlazy-inputs.md §5) — mail, notes, later messages/calendar. Triple role: (a) CANONICAL store for items that exist nowhere else (typed notes: authority 'canonical' — NEVER pruned, archived instead of deleted), (b) body cache for provider-backed items (mail: authority 'provider' — prunable; supersedes the legacy email_bodies table, which remains read-fallback until the full reset), and (c) the pending-analysis queue (status pending|analysed|error). _id is in_<msgid>_<hash(account|msg)>, the same identity scheme as events. INDEXING CAUTION: thread_id and status queries rely on non-indexed fields — fine on backends without enforced indexing; on an enforcing backend create an index on thread_id manually (the pending-queue read instead scans recent _date_modified, which is always indexed).

channel.description: mail | messages | notes | calendar | work (work = one request-and-answer turn of an agent session; the session is the thread)

item_kind.description: Finer read hint within a channel (e.g. 'meeting_notes') or null

provider.description: Who supplied it: gmail | manual | granola | slack | … (null for legacy mail captures)

account_id.description: The connection it came from, or 'manual' for typed items (part of the record's identity)

msg_id.description: The item's id within its account/source

thread_id.description: Its conversation; synthetic (note_<id>) for items without one

date.description: When it happened, unix ms (a note: the meeting time; else save/receive time)

author_address.description: The author (lowercased address; the user for manual notes)

participants.description: [{ address, name, kind }] — kind: to | cc | attendee; address may be '' for name-only attendees

participants_kind.description: recipients | attendees | channel_members — what the participants MEAN on this channel

title.description: Email subject / note title / meeting title

body_html.description: HTML body where the channel has one (mail); empty otherwise

attachments.description: [{ id, filename, mimeType, sizeBytes }] manifests — bytes stay at the provider

html_truncated.description: True when an oversized HTML body was dropped (text kept)

authority.description: canonical (we hold the ONLY copy — never pruned) | provider (cache — prunable)

archived.description: Canonical items are archived, never deleted

status.description: pending | analysed | error | skipped — the pending-analysis queue role

attempts.description: Failed-analysis count; the pending-queue drain retries an error item only while attempts < 3.

last_error.description: The most recent analysis failure (null once analysed) — shown to the user, cleared on success.

analysis_event_id.description: Back-pointer to the events record once analysed

content_hash.description: Hash of the analysed content — edit detection for synced sources

edited_asof.description: When the last revision was made (unix ms), null if never edited

prior_revisions.description: Superseded bodies of CANONICAL items: [{ revision, title, body_text, participants, date, edited_asof }] — the retention promise covers what the user wrote

linked_project_id.description: Project pre-linked at entry time (the Add-note modal picker), or null

captured_asof.description: Provider items: when the snapshot was taken

sources.description: Per-account removal tags, union-added — e.g. ['note:manual'] (same scheme as projects.sources)

accounts.description: One record per mail account: identity + where ingestion is up to — makes backfill and live ingestion resumable across restarts and job runs. The index page's is-set-up check reads this collection. Since the Slack slice one record per connection per CHANNEL (channel: mail | messages | work): a channel:'work' record (Claude Code sessions via use_file_sys) additionally carries me_email, repos { <slug>: { tracked, name } } and sessions { <sessionId>: { turns_done, last_ts, bytes, mtime, state } } — the per-session high-water marks (specs/superlazy-sessions.md).

account_id.description: The account's id within its source (archive account_id; later the connectionName)

source_id.description: The MailSource id this account is read through

cursor.description: Latest retrieved/handled message date (unix ms number) — the window-refetch watermark; kept as the fallback when sync_token expires

sync_token.description: PHASE 2: the provider's getNewer delta token for this account (null until the change-feed ingestion lands)

backfill_from.description: Unix ms (number) — start of the initial training window

history_days.description: Number — the history window used for this account's training

messages_processed.description: Number — messages analysed for this account

messages_failed.description: Number — messages whose analysis errored (recorded as error events; the cursor moves past them)

sync_paused.description: Boolean — the user paused syncing for this account (Setup page → Status → Pause syncing). While true, ingest.js resolveAccounts drops the account before the source is built and before planning, so no check (in-tab, background job, Inspect) reads it; the cursor stands still and resuming continues from it.

sync_paused_at.description: Unix ms (number) when syncing was paused; null once resumed

locks.description: ONE record ('ingestion_lock') gating ALL mail processing — training and new-mail, any tab, later the background job. Acquired ATOMICALLY (create-with-fixed-id fails if it exists), renewed by each processed message (timer-free), stale after ~5 untouched minutes, deleted on release. See specs/pipeline-walkthrough.md §2 and §11.

owner.description: Who holds it: 'tab:<random>' (later 'job:analyze_thread'). Renewal verifies ownership — a taken-over holder stops before its next message.

expires_at.description: Unix ms (number) — past this, the holder is presumed dead and the lock may be deleted + re-acquired

progress.description: { done, total, cost, latest: { subject, from_address } } — feeds the cross-page processing notice

settings.description: A single settings record (the user's app preferences). See specs/pipeline-backlog.md.

training_wip.description: Boolean — the initial history build is still in progress (all other pages redirect to the setup page while true; the setup page resumes it)

training_mode.description: live | background — how the user chose to train (background is stored as a preference; the job runner lands later)

newmail_last_check.description: Unix ms (number) — when new mail was last checked (any tab); informational

mail_action_policy.description: PHASE 2 — boolean switches for mailbox signals: { marked_read_resolves, flagged_bumps, trashed_resolves, spam_learns_sender, archive_means_done } (all default true)

history_days.description: Number — how many days back the initial history build goes

thread_context_days.description: Number — messages this recent get their COMPLETE thread as context; older ones see only the window

automated_autopilot.description: Boolean — let learned automated senders auto-process (file) without the LLM

analysis_context_chars.description: Number — INPUT budget in characters for one analysis request (assemble.js reduces by relevance to fit). Unset = 70000 (DEFAULT_CONTEXT_CHARS). The quality/cost dial on the Preferences tab.

events_retention_days.description: Number — keep events for this many days (0 = keep forever); a maintenance job prunes older ones

suggest_replies.description: Boolean — whether to draft suggested replies at all (default true)

style_guide.description: The persisted writing-style guide + regenerated every style_guide_refresh_days

style_guide_asof.description: Unix ms (number) — when style_guide was last distilled; re-built once older than style_guide_refresh_days (the cache that keeps job runs from paying a style LLM call each run)

style_guide_refresh_days.description: Number — how often to regenerate the style guide

background_mode.description: on | off — whether SuperLazy checks mail via the background job. 'on' additionally requires the job permissions AND somewhere to run (admin-trusted, or the user's serverless cloud); the UI degrades to 'off' when that is missing.

foreground_poll_minutes.description: Number — background mode ON: how often an OPEN page asks for an extra on-demand run, on top of the hourly schedule (the schedule cannot go finer than hourly).

bg_last_run.description: How the last background run went: { at, finished_at, task, version, ok, planned, processed, remaining, cost, skipped, more_pending, token_expired, error, message }. Written by the job; polled by every page — the ONLY way a page learns the outcome of a run it did not watch, because POST /jobs/run blocks for the whole run and is never awaited.

bg_last_reprofile.description: How the last background 'Update with AI' reprofile went: { at, finished_at, task, version, address, ok, outcome, reason, cost, token_expired }. Its own field (not bg_last_run) so it never clobbers an ingestion summary whose more_pending flag pages still need. The People page polls it after firing the job.

default_model.description: { provider, family } for analysis calls; null = user's freezr default

analysis_thinking.description: Whether per-message analysis lets the model reason step-by-step before answering (thinking bills as output — measured ~1,900 tokens/email when on). Default false; the bootstrap and future weekly review think regardless.

snapshot_pin.description: The PINNED catalog snapshot (cross-run provider-cache reuse): { text (the exact rendered bytes — byte-identity is what makes a cache hit possible), chars, count, ids, touched (project_ids updated since render — their current rows override the snapshot), msgs_since_render (refresh counter, ~25 triggers a re-render), rendered_asof, prompt_version (pin discarded on mismatch), pinned_asof }. One cache WRITE per refresh cycle instead of one per run.

analysis_effort.description: low | medium | high — the provider effort dial for per-message analysis (scales all output incl. reasoning). Default low. Held constant per run; changing it invalidates the cached prefix once.

business_context.description: The briefing written by the one-pass setup (and edited by the user): who the user is, their team, counterparties, rhythms and vocabulary — attached to later analysis so a model reading ONE email judges it in context

business_context_asof.description: Unix ms (number) — when the business context was last written or edited

bootstrap_asof.description: Unix ms (number) — when the one-pass setup was adopted

bootstrap_cost.description: Number — USD the one-pass setup cost, including its correction rounds

cleanup_window_days.description: Clean-up: days of input to review (default 7)

cleanup_edits_window_days.description: Clean-up: days of the user's hand edits the rules/learn sections read (default 30)

cleanup_input_mode.description: Clean-up: 'index' (one line per analysed item, all channels, bodies on request — default) or 'full' (full mail threads)

cleanup_last_run_asof.description: ms timestamp of the last clean-up run

cleanup_focus_days.description: Clean-up: days ahead the Focus section plans for (default 7)

maintenance_runs.description: One record per clean-up run (or R1 re-org) — the run-is-an-artifact principle: prompt version, knobs, input mode and window, dump/index stats, model, cost and tokens (incl. cache reads), per-section counts, suppressed count, need rounds, whether the reply was cut off.

prompt_version.description: MAINT_PROMPT_VERSION or REORG_PROMPT_VERSION for LLM runs

window.description: AI review window: { days, from, to }

dump_stats.description: { messages, threads, chars } of the dump sent

model.description: { provider, family } or {} for the user default

cost.description: total USD cost of the run (0 for deterministic runs)

project_id.description: R1 runs only: the project reviewed

incomplete.description: true when the LLM reply stopped before its done marker

suppressed.description: items dropped because the user ignored the same fingerprint earlier

cost_split.description: { input, output, other } USD — other = cache reads/writes

sizes.description: chars per block (system, state, input, closing) + estTokens — what was sent

maintenance_proposals.description: One record per clean-up ITEM — a proposal (with its ops), an attention card or a question — so decisions outlive the run: ignored is a permanent valid answer (its fingerprint suppresses the same proposal in later runs), attention cards are 'seen', questions 'dismissed', applied changes keep their audit pointer (specs/superlazy-weekly-cleanup.md §6). Housekeeping previews are NOT stored. Status is filtered client-side (only _date_modified/_id are reliably indexed).

run_id.description: the maintenance run that produced it

kind.description: the first operation's op (proposals) or the section name

data.description: the raw section payload (real ids; evidence msg ids translated)

flags.description: e.g. ['USER-EDITED profile'] - render prominently, never auto-apply

status.description: proposed | accepted | ignored | seen | dismissed | answered | applied

status_asof.description: ms timestamp of the last status change

applied_asof.description: ms timestamp when the accepted change was written

apply_error.description: why an accepted apply failed, when it did

group.description: period | focus | attention | stale | archive | merge | split | people | rules | learn | questions

title.description: the model's short title / headline / question

description.description: the model's description for the user (capped)

fingerprint.description: group + the sorted ids the ops act on — an ignored fingerprint is never shown again

evidence.description: real item ids (or hand-edit ids) the model cited

prompt_version.description: CLEANUP_PROMPT_VERSION that produced it; pending items are only re-shown at the current version

answer.description: questions: { label, index, asof } of the option chosen

llm_audit.description: DEV request audit (temporary, pruned after settings.llm_audit_days): one record per LLM exchange the per-message engine made while recording was on, plus blob records holding the cached durable turn once per distinct content. Read by the requestauditlab page; written by jobs/analyze_thread/llmAudit.js.

kind.description: 'exchange' (one LLM call) or 'blob' (a cached durable turn, id blob_<hash>)

run_id.description: the run lock owner id of the run that made the call

chain_id.description: groups the analysis call with its request_more / repair rounds

round.description: 1 for the analysis call, +1 per follow-on round

at.description: ms when the request was sent

opts.description: ask options minus the system prompt text (max_tokens, thinking, effort, cache, responseType)

turns.description: [{ role, chars, cached, text | blob }] — cached turns reference a blob by hash

error.description: error message when the call failed

meta.description: { tokensUsed, rawUsage, pricing, cost } as the server reported

text.description: blob only: the durable turn text

projects_archive.description: Archived projects — their OWN collection (user decision 2026-09-20), never loaded by the working set. Same shape as a projects record plus the archive stamps; open to-dos are cancelled on the copy at archive time. Restorable from the clean-up page.

todos.description: the project's to-dos; those open at archive time carry status cancelled with change_reason 'archived with project'

archived_reason.description: the accepted proposal's description (capped) or null

archived_run_id.description: the clean-up run whose proposal was accepted, or null
